title: Microsoft can justify higher valuation as AI demand drives Azure growth, UBS says
source_used: Proactive Investors (as carried by Yahoo Finance Canada)
key_facts: UBS raised its price target for Microsoft to $675 from $525 ahead of Microsoft's 28 Oct results.
UBS says the valuation is reasonable at 23 times estimated 2027 adjusted earnings after a 39% rally since the June-quarter results.
The market expects Azure, Microsoft's cloud business, to grow 47% in the September quarter, a potential two-point beat.
UBS cites enterprise demand, higher AI infrastructure spending, possible gains from OpenAI revenue flowing to Azure, and rising prices for hosted GPUs.
UBS lifted its valuation assumption to 25 times estimated 2028 earnings from 19 times.
Higher expectations leave less room for disappointment.
quote_evidence: UBS has raised its price target for Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT), the software and cloud computing company, to $675 from $525, arguing that strong demand for artificial intelligence services supports higher growth expectations ahead of its 28 October results.

The revised target reflects growing confidence in the company's ability to monetise artificial intelligence while maintaining profitability, although the higher expectations leave less room for disappointment in its upcoming results.
why_it_matters_hint: A bank bets that AI-driven cloud demand will carry Microsoft's results.
